content.thinking:
This text is expository, walking through how scientists measure climate through ice cores, satellites, and CO2 observatories, using vivid analogies like a drop of ink in an Olympic pool. It leans heavily on competence and rigor rather than integrity or benevolence, without addressing skepticism or funding motives directly, so I'd expect it to boost competence trust modestly while leaving other dimensions less affected.

Working through the anchored ratings, I'm landing around +1.9 for trust_multidimensional (competence-driven), smaller anchored shifts for trust_post (~1.2) and distrust_post (-0.9), and modest positive nudges for funding_perceptions (+0.8), policy_role (+1.0), and institutional trust given the NASA mention (+0.9). The remaining measures — belief, concern, policy support, behavior, and donation likelihood — get smaller positive bumps since the piece focuses on measurement and evidence rather than direct calls to action or emotional appeals.

parsed_output.reasoning_summary: This arm is a purely expository 'how climate science works' text: instrumentation, ice cores, volcanic-ash dating, isotopes, satellite CO2 retrievals with a vivid precision analogy. Its main mechanism is competence/rigor signaling (methodological transparency), which should lift the competence and openness subscales of the multidimensional battery more than integrity/benevolence, so the four-subscale mean is diluted; there is no messenger, no motive/funding defense, and no explicit correction of skeptic claims, so it should land near the middle of the 16 arms rather than at the top (~+1.9 on the primary). The pre-measured single items (trust_post, belief_post) are anchored and get roughly 60% of the fresh battery's effect. The text does implicitly justify continued research and names NASA, giving small positive effects on funding perceptions and institutional trust (diluted by the federal-government item), and it closes by linking findings to international assessments and mitigation, giving modest spillover to policy_role and small effects on belief, concern, and policy. Distal outcomes (specific policies, behavioral intentions) get well under half a point, and incentivized outcomes get near-zero shifts: a few cents to the AMS (topically congruent with meteorological measurement) and under one percentage point on newsletter sign-up.
